title: Seasonal Asynchrony of Microbial Biomass and Respiration Across Terrestrial Ecosystems
content:
Integrating global datasets and site-level observations, we show that periods of higher microbial biomass do not coincide with higher respiration. This asynchrony reflects divergent drivers; biomass tracks plant competition and respiration tracks temperature. Our results offer correlative evidence to refine microbial carbon dynamics in Earth system models.


ABSTRACT

Soil microorganisms are fundamental drivers of terrestrial carbon cycling, acting both as a major reservoir of carbon through their biomass and as a dominant flux via respiration. While conventional models assume a positive correlation between microbial biomass and respiration at the interannual scale, the seasonal synchrony between these two components remains poorly understood. Here, we analyzed seasonal data from 323 studies to assess the synchrony between microbial biomass carbon and respiration, and used site-level observations to explore the underlying mechanisms. We observed a seasonal asynchrony between microbial biomass and respiration, meaning that periods of higher biomass did not consistently coincide with higher respiration rates. This seasonal asynchrony was consistent with divergent governing mechanisms, in which microbial biomass was associated with plant competition, whereas microbial respiration was closely associated with temperature. Our findings provide correlative evidence to refine microbial-mediated carbon seasonal dynamics in Earth system models under increasing climatic seasonality.
